description: A product or service that a visitor signs up to or starts using (SaaS, membership, app).

journey.audience: <who is doing the journey, and what they need>
journey.endsAt: The first next-step screen. Nothing is submitted.

stages.name: Arrive and orient
stages.task: You land here with this need. What do you do first?
checks: The first screen says in plain words what this is

stages.name: Understand the offer
stages.task: You want to know how this works. Where do you look?
checks: How it works is shown as steps
Cost or commitment is visible, or how it's decided
What is and isn't included is one click away

stages.name: Choose your route
stages.task: You fit this group. Where do you go?
checks: Visitors can pick a route by role or need
Route labels use the visitors' own words (check against Forum findings)
No more than 5 routes in one group (a house rule, not a law)

stages.name: Start
stages.task: You want to begin. Where do you click?
checks: The first next-step screen is 3 clicks or fewer from arrival (a house rule)
The first screen asks only for what it needs
The next step and how long it takes are stated

stages.name: Reassurance
stages.task: Before going further, you want to know you can trust this. Where do you look?
checks: Independent proof sits near the decision, with its source named
Who stands behind it is stated
Help or contact is visible at decision points
